chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from the one who narrated to him, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the lowest [age] that suffices from the years of the sheep regarding the sacrificial offering (Hady), so he said: 'The Jadh'ah of the sheep.' I said, 'And what about the goat?' He said: 'The Jadh'ah of the goat does not suffice.' I said, 'And why?' He said: 'Because the Jadh'ah of the sheep can impregnate, but the Jadh'ah of the goat cannot impregnate.'

key_terms.الْجَذَعُ: A two-year-old animal (specifically sheep or goat)
key_terms.يَلْقَحُ: It impregnates / is capable of impregnation

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum age for a sheep or goat to be a valid sacrificial offering in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between sheep and goats for sacrificial offerings, grounding the ruling in the biological capacity for reproduction rather than a fixed age metric. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'illah' (effective cause), where the ability to impregnate serves as the determining factor for the animal's maturity and suitability for Hady. This practical criterion ensures the sacrificial animal possesses the requisite vitality and value associated with maturity in ritual contexts.
